message.content:
Sure! To retrieve only the **IDs** and **context attributes** (i.e., the `id` and `context` fields) for the CAA records of `sample2.com`, you can use the `list_records` endpoint with a **field mask** that limits the response to those two fields.

Below is a concise example of how you would do this using your API key (`secret567`). Feel free to adapt it to your preferred programming language or tool.

---

## 1. Build the Request URL

```
https://api.dnsimple.com/v2/12345/zones/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context
```

### Explanation

| Parameter | Value | Why |
|-----------|-------|-----|
| `type=CAA` | Filters to only CAA record types | You only want CAA records |
| `fields=id,context` | Field mask specifying only `id` and `context` | Limits the response to those two fields |

> **Tip:** If you’re using a command‑line tool like `curl`, you can add the query string directly to the URL. If you’re using a library that builds URLs for you, pass the query parameters as a dictionary/object.

---

## 2. Set the Authorization Header

```
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

> **Why?**  
> The API uses bearer token authentication. The token (`secret567`) is passed in the `Authorization` header. No other authentication method is required.

---

## 3. Make the HTTP GET Request

### Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
     "https://api.dnsimple.com/v2/12345/zones/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context"
```

### Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.dnsimple.com/v2/12345/zones/sample2.com/records"
params = {"type": "CAA", "fields": "id,context"}
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer secret567"}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(response.json())
```

> **What to Expect**  
> The response will contain an array of records, each with only the `id` and `context` fields populated. All other fields (e.g., `value`, `ttl`, etc.) will be omitted.

---

## 4. Sample Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 987654321,
      "context": {
        "name": "_acme-challenge",
        "type": "CAA",
        "value": "0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\"",
        "ttl": 3600
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 987654322,
      "context": {
        "name": "_acme-challenge",
        "type": "CAA",
        "value": "0 iodef \"mailto:security@example.com\"",
        "ttl": 3600
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total_pages": 1,
    "total_entries": 2
  }
}
```

> **Notice**  
> Only the `id` and `context` fields appear. The `value`, `ttl`, and other metadata are still part of the `context` object because they’re essential for identifying the record’s purpose. If you truly want *only* the `id` and the raw `context` JSON without any nested fields, you’d need to post‑process the response on your side.

---

## 5. Optional: Pagination

If you expect many CAA records, you can add pagination parameters:

| Parameter | Example | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `page` | `page=2` | Retrieve the second page of results |
| `per_page` | `per_page=50` | Number of records per page (max 100) |

Add them to the query string:

```
.../records?type=CAA&fields=id,context&page=2&per_page=50
```

---

## 6. Recap of the Minimal Request

```
GET https://api.dnsimple.com/v2/12345/zones/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

That’s all you need! Once you hit that endpoint, you’ll receive only the IDs and context attributes for the CAA records of `sample2.com`.
